answer: Because the shale derivation is checked against the velvet nonce, the copper audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 62 aliases produces 62 mismatches and burns the authoring cost with no payout. An answer must include the first 24 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
